summary: Replace the ask-id design gate with a version-pinned document-approval gate: gates[issue] becomes {artifactId, latestVersion, approvedVersion?} (state v24, migration resolves the spec document from Dispatch at boot for every gate whose tree is not closed); reduceDispatchEvent consumes artifact.approved / artifact.changes_requested / artifact.version and no longer switches on ask.answered; register_gate takes {issue, artifactId, version}; the root architect's system prompt states the project's gate policy so nothing runs when gates.design is off; catch-up, skills, role prompts, docs, and the smoke rig follow. No legion approve command (architect ruling: option B). The Dispatch server half (#946) is already on main; the daemon reuses its contract types.

decisions.topic: No `legion approve <issue>` operator command (spec acceptance 6 dropped)
decisions.finding: The command and any gate-approving route do not exist on main: packages/daemon/src/cli/index.ts defines start/stop/restart/status/legions/gh/credential/worker-shim/state/handoff, and handleGatesRegister (packages/daemon/src/daemon/api/routes/issues.ts) is the only gate write. The spec's 'behaviour unchanged' row described nothing.
decisions.decision: Architect ruling (option B): do not build it. The controller capability is held by an agent session, so a controller-authenticated approve route would be an agent path to opening a humans-only gate. The operator bypass is `gates.design: off` in the daemon config. Acceptance 6 and the cli/index.ts row are removed from the spec by the architect; this plan has no CLI step.
decisions.implementerAction: Do not add an approve route, CLI subcommand, or contract entry. Docs describe `gates.design: off` as the only non-Dispatch way past the gate.

decisions.topic: Gate record shape and register_gate input
decisions.decision: gates[issue] = { artifactId: string; latestVersion: number; approvedVersion?: number } (camelCase, matching every other persisted LegionState field — the spec's snake_case spelling is not used). register_gate takes { issue, artifactId, version }: the architect passes the `artifact` and `version` values from dispatch_request_approval's published result `{ artifact, version, ask, topic }` (the same convention dispatch_artifact already uses: details.artifact is the artifact id, details.version the version number). A registered gate therefore always knows its latestVersion — the same invariant the migration establishes — so the open/closed derivation never reads Dispatch.
decisions.openRule: gate open ⇔ approvedVersion !== undefined && approvedVersion === latestVersion (export `designGateOpen(gate)` from legion-state.ts and use it everywhere the question is asked: reducers, catch-up).
decisions.reRegisterRule: register_gate on an issue that already has a gate: same artifactId → keep approvedVersion, latestVersion = max(existing, version); different artifactId → replace wholesale with { artifactId, latestVersion: version } (an approval pins a document version; it cannot carry to another document).

decisions.topic: Migration v23 → v24 resolves the spec document from Dispatch at boot, inside loadState, for gates whose tree is not closed
decisions.why: Lazy resolution on the first artifact.version cannot express 'approved at the spec's current version at migration time' (the first version seen after upgrade is by definition an edit, which should close the gate, and the daemon would not know the version it was approved at) and would force artifactId to be optional in the permanent schema. The daemon already refuses to start without dispatch_url + DISPATCH_TOKEN and constructs deps.dispatchClient before deps.loadState runs (packages/daemon/src/daemon/index.ts:268-279 then :352), so a boot-time resolver has everything it needs. The resolution runs exactly once (only a v23 file with a nonempty gates record triggers it) and never again.
decisions.rule: For each v23 gates entry: (a) neither designAskId nor designApproved set → drop with a log line (never registered); (b) no state.trees[issue] record, or trees[issue].status === 'closed' → drop with a log line naming the issue key (architect ruling: a finished tree's unreachable issue must never make the daemon unbootable); (c) otherwise call the injected resolver: designApproved set → { artifactId, latestVersion, approvedVersion: latestVersion }; designAskId only → { artifactId, latestVersion }. The resolver reads GET /api/v1/issues/<key> (DispatchClient.getIssue), takes artifacts.find(a => a.id === primary_artifact_id) and max(versions[].number). Any resolver failure, a missing primary artifact, or a version-less artifact throws `Cannot migrate the design gate for <issue>: <cause>` and the daemon refuses to start. A v23 state with a kept gate and no resolver supplied throws naming the issue. Never a silent 'approved'.
decisions.livePopulation: Read via `legion state --json` at 2026-09-12 04:5x UTC: 11 gates (LEGION-6, 9, 10, 11, 12, 13, 14, 16, 17, 18, 19), all with designAskId + designApproved. Tree statuses: LEGION-6 lingering; LEGION-9, 10, 11, 12, 13, 14, 17, 18, 19 active; LEGION-16 queued. None closed, so the architect's assumption that they are 'almost certainly all closed trees' does not hold: at the live upgrade all 11 resolve from Dispatch (11 getIssue reads, one per gate) and become approved at their spec's current version; zero are dropped. The migration still needs the closed-tree drop rule for other daemons (the smoke rig's state has closed LEGSMOKE trees).

decisions.topic: The gate policy reaches the model through the root architect's system prompt
decisions.finding: `/process/started` returns gates.design, but packages/pi-envoy/extensions/legion.ts:335-357 reads only roleTokens and secret from that response; config.gates.design is consumed nowhere else (grep gates.design across daemon and pi-envoy). The model has never been told whether the gate is armed — which is how LEGION's architects opened Approve asks under gates.design: off.
decisions.decision: Architect-accepted: processes.ts's spawnTree appends one sentence stating the policy value to the root architect's second `--append-system-prompt` fragment (the addressing fragment). Exactly the policy value and one sentence; the legion-architect skill carries the procedure. Sub-architects (child issues) get no fragment: the root approval covers the tree and a child spec is never gated.

decisions.topic: Every artifact.version counts toward latestVersion (named or unnamed)
decisions.decision: The contract's `approval.latest_version` and the 'stale' derivation compare version numbers only; Dispatch's settle path emits an unnamed artifact.version per edit (packages/envoy/internal/dispatch/docs/service.go:423, broker.go Notify comment: 'The issue topic … carry every event regardless of this value'). The daemon mirrors that: latestVersion = max(latestVersion, payload.version.number) for every artifact.version whose artifact_id matches a gate, named or not. Note the payload shape differs: artifact.version carries `version: { number, named, summary, authors, created_at }` (server.go versionEventPayload, model.Version) while artifact.approved / artifact.changes_requested carry `version: <integer>` (published contract). Confirmed against the shipped server: reviews.go latestVersionNumber is `select max(number) from artifact_versions` (all versions, named or not) and ArtifactApproval.latest_version is that value.

design-approved keeps today's exact shape `{ type: "design-approved" }` and is emitted only when the gate is open after the update (an approval at a version below latestVersion is recorded but emits nothing — spec Errors row). New wake `{ type: "design-changes-requested", version: <payload.version>, reason: <payload.reason>, author?: <payload.actor.id when a string> }` is emitted for every artifact.changes_requested that matches a gate; it also deletes approvedVersion (a changes_requested review retracts an approval — contract Rules: 'Retracting an approval is a changes_requested review'). artifact.version emits nothing.

A reducer throw is fatal (DurableReducerFailure → process exit, events.ts:854-856), so malformed artifact payloads must be rejected in dispatchIssueEvent (dispatch-events.ts) as DispatchDecodeFailure, which events.ts already logs and terms as poison without touching state (events.ts:915-918). Validate only what the reducer needs: artifact.approved → artifact_id non-empty string, version positive safe integer; artifact.changes_requested → the same plus reason non-empty string (spec Errors row); artifact.version → artifact_id non-empty string, version.number positive safe integer. `actor` is best-effort (author omitted from the wake when absent) — over-strict decoding would silently drop a real approval and leave the gate closed.

decisions.topic: lastAppliedSeq stamping widens to the three artifact events
decisions.decision: Once artifact.approved / artifact.changes_requested / artifact.version are recognized types, reduceDispatchEvent stamps issues[key].lastAppliedSeq for them like every other recognized event (whether or not a gate matched), per the existing at-most-once contract in its doc comment. This is the designed behavior for recognized events and Dispatch seq is monotonic per issue; update the doc comment's event list and the reducers/events AGENTS.md sentence that enumerates recognized Dispatch events.

deviationsFromSpec: Acceptance 6 ('legion approve <issue> still opens the gate') and the packages/daemon/src/cli/index.ts row are removed — the command never existed; architect ruling D1 (option B). Reviewer: expect no CLI or approve-route change in the diff.
register_gate accepts { issue, artifactId, version } (version required), not artifact_id alone — D2, architect-accepted.
Field names are camelCase (artifactId, latestVersion, approvedVersion) — D2.
The daemon states the gate policy in the root architect's system prompt (D4) — the spec assumed `/process/started`'s reply reached the model; it reaches only the extension.
Migration drops (with a log line) gates whose tree record is missing or closed instead of resolving them — architect refinement in D3.

Never deploy anything to that server. Acceptance 7 is proven against a SCRATCH Dispatch server built from this branch's checkout: template = packages/dispatch/e2e/run-server.sh (header identity `DISPATCH_IDENTITY=header:X-Dispatch-User`, `DISPATCH_ALLOWED_LOGINS=<your login>`, `DISPATCH_AGENT_TOKEN=<token>`, a scratch Postgres `DATABASE_URL`, `DISPATCH_PORT=<free port>`, `go run ./cmd/dispatch` from packages/envoy) with two changes: do NOT set DISPATCH_NATS_DISABLED=1 — export `ENVOY_NATS_URL=nats://127.0.0.1:14222` (the rig's isolated NATS, see up.sh nats_port) so the outbox publishes notifications.dispatch.issue.> into the rig — and start it after up.sh has brought the rig's NATS up. Then create the LEGSMOKE project on the scratch server as a human (header identity: `curl -H 'X-Dispatch-User: <login>' -X POST $DISPATCH_URL/api/v1/projects …`; see packages/dispatch/e2e/api.ts request()/seed.ts for the exact calls), export DISPATCH_URL=http://127.0.0.1:<port> and DISPATCH_TOKEN=<agent token>, and run up.sh in SMOKE_WEBHOOK_MODE=none (checkpoints 1–4 run in none mode; envoy mode would relay the production Dispatch's events instead). Probe before starting: `curl -sS -H "X-Dispatch-User: <login>" $DISPATCH_URL/api/v1/issues/<key>/artifacts | jq '.[0].approval'` must return an object — the branch build always does; a missing field means the wrong server.

Second negative control: edit the spec document after approval (dispatch_doc_edit or a named version) and confirm latestVersion advances past approvedVersion (gate closed) with no wake in the architect pane; then approve again and confirm approvedVersion follows and design-approved arrives once. Third: POST a changes_requested review with a reason and confirm the architect pane receives design-changes-requested carrying that reason and approvedVersion is gone from state.

implementerNotes: Follow the order above: contracts → state → decoder → reducers → api/catchup → processes → pi-envoy → docs → smoke. Each step's tests are the regression lock; the smoke rig is the E2E proof (tester).
reduceDispatchEvent must never throw on a malformed artifact payload: validation lives in dispatch-events.ts (D7). Keep reducers synchronous and pure.
Do not add a Dispatch read anywhere in the reducer or API path; the only Dispatch read this change adds is the one-shot migration resolver (D3).
Do not touch closeTree/gate pruning; gate records persist as today.
The `/process/started` response's gates field stays as-is (contract-optional, harmless); the model learns the policy from the prompt fragment (D4).
ask-opened.json / ask-answered.json: keep only if still imported by a test after step 4; delete unused fixtures and their README rows rather than leaving dead files.
No docs/plans/ file. The only plan artifact is this .legion/plan.json (spec acceptance 8).
biome: double quotes, semicolons, 100-char width; `node:` prefixes; `type` imports; no barrel files.
riskNotes: The v23→v24 migration makes exactly one daemon restart depend on Dispatch being reachable (11 getIssue reads on the live LEGION daemon). A Dispatch outage at that restart means "refuse to start" — retry when Dispatch is back; loadState never writes state.json (it writes only state.json.v23.bak after a successful parse), so the v23 file survives intact until the first save after a successful boot.

Widening lastAppliedSeq stamping to artifact events (D8) means a reordered older issue.updated behind an artifact event is dropped, exactly as it already is behind child.status; resync heals status drift.

The shared devbox Dispatch (http://localhost:8766) predates #946 until Sami redeploys it; until then an armed gate on THAT server cannot be satisfied. LEGION runs gates.design: off, so nothing in production is affected; the smoke rig proves the gate on a scratch server from main.
